issue_context.title: `require.context` not parsed in ESM packages
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->
<!-- Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of webpack. -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the webpack Gitter. -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- https://gitter.im/webpack/webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**

In packages with `type: "module"`, webpack fails to parse and replace `require.context()` expressions.

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

1. Clone https://github.com/tavoyne/webpack-2ece8c.
2. Run `yarn webpack --mode=production`.
3. Inspect the `dist/main.js` file and notice that the `require.context()` expression is still present.
4. (Remove `type: "module"` from the `package.json` file.)
5. (Inspect the `dist/main.js` file again and notice how the `require.context()` expression was successfully replaced.)

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**

The replacement to be successful at step (3).

As `require` is not available in ESM environments, it could be called `import.context` in order to avoid confusion.

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version:  `5.68.0`
Node.js version: `17.4.0`
Operating System: MacOS
Additional tools: N/A
comments:
Thanks for your issue. This done intentionally since in esm there is no `require`, you can mark this js file as `type="javascript/auto"` in your `webpack.config`( use https://webpack.js.org/configuration/module/#ruletype )

Ah.. if you need `context` you still can use `import('/a/a' + name)` https://webpack.js.org/api/module-methods/#dynamic-expressions-in-import

I understand, but the fact that it's called `require.context` is anecdotical, isn't it? I mean Webpack doesn't use the `require` function under the hood, it just parses the expression. In this case it's a shame to restrict its usage to CJS environments only, don't you think?

> Ah.. if you need context you still can use import('/a/a' + name)

I agree this is handy, but I need the filenames.
Webpack tries to follow specs. Since esm kind of strict environment there is no cjs stuff in it.
But `require.context` is not a _cjs stuff_, it's webpack's.

`require.context` exists only because webpack starts when ESM was not ready, so `require.context` is just hack for `import(...)`, because currently ESM is preferable and we should reduce usage of commonjs, we stop to add new features for `require` (i.e. CommonJS) and also block them to ESM
Unless I'm missing something here, it could have been called `webpack.context` or `blabla` and work the same way. The fact that it has `require` in it is arbitrary.
I agree with you @alexander-akait. But `require.context()` has an extra functionality compared to `import()`: it's the fact that you can access filenames.

@vankop @tavoyne To be honest, I have quite different feelings, on the one hand, I understand well how it is used and why it is needed, on the other hand, we already had the experience of adding new stuff to module system and it always ended badly.

It changes `import` logic, it is very bad idea, we should not do it, in this case better to use `import.meta.context()`, because `import.meta.*` is free to use, maybe even `import.meta.webpackContent` to prevent overlapping with other tools
Makes complete sense. Could work on a PR if it's something that you'd consider integrating.

`import.meta.webpackContext` would be the name to choose here.

But we should use the chance to improve the API a bit and let it take an object instead of many arguments. This would also allow to add the other options a context takes, like `include` or `exclude` or `mode`
similar phenomenon was found when using [require.resolveWeak](https://webpack.js.org/api/module-methods/#requireresolveweak) in a pure ESM package @sokra @alexander-akait
